title: Strict augmented quotient descent along an open
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, schemes V,W in a universe independent of E, and an open immersion e:V→W. For an adic coefficient datum on its valuation ring whose ideal is generated by the chosen uniformizer [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], every operation presentation o [def-sf-integral-open-operations] admits a StrictComparison [def-sf-augmented-strict-integral-completion]. In detail, the finite and completed coefficient maps are isomorphisms and preserve transitions; exact restriction preserves flat-term K-flat complexes; balanced tensor restriction gives one natural isomorphism of strict quotient complexes with its local pure-tensor and transition formulas; it descends to a natural derived strict-tower isomorphism tau with the universal computation-counit normalization and the actual strict augmentation square. No inverse-limit or ordinary pullback comparison is asserted. Exponent index n denotes n+1; no boundedness, completeness or quasi-compactness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Use the localized pro-etale site equivalence. Under it the inverse image $e^{-1}$ of sheaves of sets, abelian groups and rings is restriction to the slice, naturally in the sheaf [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction, clause 1]; so the coefficient isomorphisms $c_{e,n},c_e$, stated for $e^{-1}$, become $(A_n)_W|_V\cong(A_n)_V$ and $B_W|_V\cong B_V$ with the same projection and transition equations. Use the supplied operation presentation and regard $e^*$ as restriction with coefficient ring $B_W|_V=B_V$. The finite identifications preserve $1$, all quotient transitions and the projections from $B$. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $H$. Exactness of restriction makes $e^*P$ represent $e^*H$; K-flat pullback makes it K-flat with flat terms. Change of rings therefore computes every reduction by $P\otimes_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and its restricted analogue, without a boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case, (2),(5) and proof of (5); strict augmentation refinement using sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0G7E and 07A4.

proof.text: Apply the algebraic inverse-image tensor comparison at each degree of $P$ and each $n$, with the coefficient identifications of Step 1. It gives a chain isomorphism $e^*(P\otimes_{B_W}(A_n)_W)\cong(e^*P)\otimes_{B_V}(A_n)_V$, sending a restricted pure tensor to the same pure tensor; its inverse does likewise. The differential is $d_P\otimes1$, so the tensor comparison commutes with it. Reading the two sides as $B_V$-modules uses precisely the projection compatibility of the coefficient isomorphisms. Thus these are comparisons of the required scalar-restricted complexes, not just of their underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case, (2),(5) and proof of (5); strict augmentation refinement using sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0G7E and 07A4.

proof.text: Let $r_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$ denote reduction. Both composites in the transition square send $x\otimes a$ to the restricted $x\otimes r_n(a)$; both composites in the augmentation square send $x$ to $x\otimes1$. These equalities on local pure tensors are equalities of sheaf maps by the tensor universal property. Consequently Step 2 is an isomorphism of strict augmented towers, with source the pulled strict augmentation and target the strict quotient augmentation of $e^*P$. The formulas also commute with every cochain map $P\to P'$.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case, (2),(5) and proof of (5); strict augmentation refinement using sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0G7E and 07A4.

proof.text: To pass to derived strict towers, use the equivalence between the localization of flat-term K-flat representatives and $D(B_W)$. A quasi-isomorphism between good representatives induces a quasi-isomorphism at every quotient level by derived change of rings. These form one strict tower map, and it is a quasi-isomorphism in the tower category because kernels, cokernels and hence cohomology are levelwise. The same holds after exact restriction. The natural strict isomorphism of Steps 2--3 therefore descends through that localization to $\tau_H$, natural for all derived morphisms, and independent of representatives via the canonical computation comparisons. Its augmented squares descend with it. This uses whole strict maps before localization, rather than attempting to lift a family of unrelated derived-level maps.

theorem openStrictQuotientDescent
    (_d : AdicCoefficientDatum (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))
    (_hd : _d.ideal = Ideal.span {Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E}) :
    Nonempty (StrictComparison l E e o)
